page: Microsoft Azure F4ams_v6 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the Famsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, but it is premium storage capable, allowing high-performance external disk attachments.

In benchmark evaluations, the F4ams_v6 demonstrates strong single-core performance, as evidenced by its top-tier results in stress-ng single-core CPU tests and Geekbench single-core scores. Text processing and single-threaded bzip3 decompression also rank in the top 25% of tested servers. Multi-core performance, including Geekbench multi-core and stress-ng multi-core metrics, falls within the average range. Memory performance is mixed; while read-only small-block cached memory bandwidth is average at 592.54 GB/sec, large-block uncached read bandwidth is weak at 38.92 GB/sec. Large-block write bandwidth remains average at 28.0 GB/sec.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and strong single-threaded execution capabilities, the F4ams_v6 is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring high memory density without massive parallel compute requirements. It is well-suited for database operations, text processing, and lightweight language model text generation using small models, where it achieves strong performance. However, due to weak uncached large-block read memory bandwidth and lower multi-threaded scaling, it is less optimal for memory-bound large-dataset streaming or heavy multi-threaded parallel processing.
description: Microsoft Azure F4ams_v6 is a memory-intensive virtual machine from the Famsv6 family, powered by a dedicated 4-core AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. Built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this x86_64 server features 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It lacks local storage and GPUs but supports premium storage configurations. Benchmarks show strong single-core CPU execution, text processing, and small-model text generation, though multi-core performance and uncached large-block read memory bandwidth are average to weak. This hardware profile makes the F4ams_v6 highly suitable for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and single-threaded processing tasks where high memory density is required without the overhead of excessive CPU cores.
